title: Two Huangs Don’t Make A Right
text:
Two Huangs Don’t Make A Right

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 12 Nov 2026

I am old enough to remember the “spy balloon” crisis of February 2023. A few weeks before Antony Blinken was set for his inaugural visit to Beijing as Secretary of State, a frenzy gripped US media over a Chinese “surveillance balloon” flying over the United States (we will park the fact that China already has an estimated 1,687 satellites in space, most of which can probably take better pictures of America’s corn fields than an unmanned helium balloon?). Blinken’s visit was duly canceled (see Deflating Expectations For US-China Relations).A couple of years later, Donald Trump was back in power and set to meet with Xi Jinping in Busan, South Korea. A few days before the summit, the US Commerce Department decided to expand the sanctions entity list and pushed the number of sanctioned Chinese firms from 1,500 to 20,000.
